cards.design_implication: Designs requiring comparable SN Ia distance measurements should include a procedure for calibrating peak magnitudes via lightcurve width (e.g., stretch factor) and applying color-based K-corrections to align observed bands with restframe bands.
does_not_establish: The exact mathematical form of the width-luminosity relation constants.
Whether this calibration applies to other classes of supernovae.
cards.evidence_excerpt: All supernova peak magnitudes are standardized using a SN Ia lightcurve width-luminosity relation.
limitations: The text specifies the standardization method but does not provide the specific coefficients or uncertainties for the relation beyond the general description.
This calibration is specific to Type Ia supernovae.
cards.statement: The study standardizes Type Ia supernova peak magnitudes using a lightcurve width-luminosity relation and applies cross-filter K-corrections based on supernova color and template spectra.

cards.design_implication: If designing a study to measure cosmological parameters via magnitude-redshift relations, one should explicitly define the statistical error budget to include intrinsic magnitude dispersion and redshift uncertainty from peculiar velocities.
does_not_establish: The theoretical minimum achievable dispersion for SNe Ia.
Global or local peculiar velocity models beyond the simplified 300 km/s assumption.
cards.evidence_excerpt: The two sources of statistical error that are common to all the supernovae are the intrinsic dispersion of SN Ia luminosities after correcting for the width-luminosity relation, taken as 0.17 mag, and the redshift uncertainty due to peculiar velocities, which are taken as 300 km $\mathbf { s } ^ { - 1 }$ .
limitations: The values (0.17 mag, 300 km/s) are specific to the sample and analysis conditions of this study.
This does not establish the best practice for all future studies, only what was used here.
cards.statement: The analysis treats intrinsic dispersion and peculiar velocities as primary sources of statistical error, with intrinsic dispersion taken as 0.17 mag and peculiar velocity uncertainty as 300 km/s.

cards.design_implication: Designs aiming to constrain cosmological parameters via supernovae should consider a joint fit approach that combines high-redshift samples with lower-redshift calibration samples to simultaneously determine nuisance parameters like absolute magnitude.
does_not_establish: The statistical power gained by this specific combination compared to other combinations.
The independence of the high- and low-redshift datasets.
cards.evidence_excerpt: The magnitude-redshift data for these supernovae, at redshifts between 0.18 and 0.83, are fit jointly with a set of supernovae from the Calán/Tololo Supernova Survey, at redshifts below 0.1, to yield values for the cosmological parameters.
limitations: The design is specific to the supernova datasets available at the time of publication.
Does not establish the optimal redshift range for future missions.
cards.statement: The cosmological parameters were determined by fitting magnitude-redshift data from 42 high-redshift Type Ia supernovae jointly with a set of low-redshift supernovae from the Calán/Tololo Supernova Survey.

cards.design_implication: Research objects for measuring cosmological density parameters using this method must be Type Ia supernovae with observable lightcurves sufficient to determine width and peak magnitude.
does_not_establish: That other objects (e.g., CMB, BAO) cannot measure these parameters.
The precision of the measurement for individual supernovae versus the sample.
cards.evidence_excerpt: We report measurements of the mass density, $\Omega _ { \mathrm { M } } ,$ , and cosmological-constant energy density, $\Omega _ { \Lambda }$ , of the universe based on the analysis of 42 Type Ia supernovae discovered by the Supernova Cosmology Project.
limitations: This claim is specific to the Type Ia supernovae class.
The measurability depends on the distance to the supernova allowing precise photometric measurement.
cards.statement: The study measures the mass density ($\Omega_M$) and cosmological-constant energy density ($\Omega_\Lambda$) based on the analysis of Type Ia supernovae peak magnitudes standardized by lightcurve width.
